requirement_text.REQ-378: See handoffs/WF03-ISS0736-20260921/step-00-git-setup.json context.requirement_text.REQ-378 for the full verbatim text. Acceptance criteria: (1) a tenant_admin action revoking a signed-in business_user's access takes effect on that user's very next request with no sign-out/reload/token-expiry wait, demonstrated by a revoke-then-immediately-retry test with no sleep/token refresh; (2) the revoking action is reachable through Letflow's own web/ GUI, not only Keycloak; (3) the resulting 403 renders through the existing QueryStateBoundary/PermissionDenied contract unchanged, no new renderer state, no leaked content; (4) SECURITY-REVIEWER signs off explicitly on the chosen enforcement mechanism before merge.

task.description: Hard gate on lib/letflow/design/req378-oidc-live-revocation-check.md. Verify every one of REQ-378's 4 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete, unambiguous design element (see requirement_text.REQ-378 above). Specifically check: (1) the live per-request revocation check (status + roles) is precisely specified -- exact function, exact query, exact short-circuit point in AuthPipeline.authenticate_oidc/2's pipeline, exact denial status code with reasoning; (2) the GUI reachability claim (existing GroupsPage.tsx member-removal / UserDetailPage.tsx status-change endpoints) is verified against the actual current source of those files and actually already write what the new backend check reads, not merely asserted; (3) the AC3 no-renderer-change claim is checked against actual QueryStateBoundary/PermissionDenied source; (4) confirm the design contains no .ex/.tsx implementation bodies, only signatures/types/schema shapes; (5) confirm gap 3 (client-side role staleness) is explicitly stated as out of scope, not silently left ambiguous; (6) resolve or explicitly flag-for-REVIEWER the design's own two open questions (403 vs 401 for inactive accounts; reliance on evaluate_access/2's existing empty-role-list behavior) -- a validator PASS must not wave through an unresolved open question without at least confirming it is safe to defer and naming who resolves it next (REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER).

result.summary: Independently re-verified all source claims in lib/letflow/design/req378-oidc-live-revocation-check.md against actual current source (not the design doc's own assertions): auth_pipeline.ex's authenticate_oidc/2 with-chain (lines 126-132) confirmed to match §1's insertion-point claim; users.status Ecto.Enum(:active/:inactive) confirmed at identity/user.ex:41; RoleRegistry's verbatim no-coupling moduledoc quote confirmed at role_registry.ex:11-17; the group_members/tenant_role join shape confirmed to support §2.1's proposed query; TenantProvisioning.schema_name_for_tenant/1 confirmed pure/no-I/O; Authorization.has_permission?([], _) confirmed to fall through to Deny403 via Enum.any?([],...) == false, supporting the design's empty-role-list open question as safe; QueryStateBoundary/classifyError.ts/PermissionDenied.tsx confirmed to classify 401/403 by HTTP status only with no server-reason branching and no leaked content (AC3 holds). AC2's UserDetailPage.tsx deactivation path (both the status-select 'Save' path and the dedicated 'Deactivate' button, via useAdminUsers.ts) independently confirmed to both call usersApi.update -> PATCH /api/v1/users/:id -> routers/identity.ex handle_patch/3 -> Identity.update_user_profile/3, exactly as designed -- that half of AC2 is correct. FAIL is on AC2's role-revocation half: the design's §4 table claims GroupsPage.tsx's removeMember.mutate -> groupsApi.removeMembers(groupId, [userId]) reaches DELETE /groups/:id/members/:user_id -> Identity.remove_group_member/3. Independently reading web/src/api/identity.ts:55-58 shows removeMembers(id, userIds) explicitly discards userIds (`void userIds`) and calls client.delete(`/api/v1/admin/groups/${id}/members`) -- no user_id segment, /admin/ prefix, and client.delete (web/src/api/client.ts:250-252) sends no body, so the target member is never identified. Cross-checked against the actual backend mount (lib/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline.ex:141 mounts Letflow.Routers.Identity at /identity, so the real route is /api/v1/identity/groups/:id/members/:user_id, routers/identity.ex:182) -- no backend route matches /api/v1/admin/groups/:id/members at all (the design's own table also mis-cites the route as /groups/:id/members/:user_id, omitting the /identity mount prefix). The GroupsPage.tsx 'Remove' button is therefore not wired to the endpoint the design relies on for AC2's role-revocation half; the design's premise ('no web/ change is required for AC2') is false for this half. Per WF-02 Step 1b, a design that asserts an already-verified GUI write path which is independently found not to match the real source fails immediately and completely -- no partial credit.

issues.description: Design §4's GUI-reachability table claims GroupsPage.tsx's per-member 'Remove' button (removeMember.mutate -> groupsApi.removeMembers(groupId, [userId])) reaches DELETE /groups/:id/members/:user_id -> Identity.remove_group_member/3, which would delete the group_members row the new verify_local_account_state/2 step reads. Independently verified false: web/src/api/identity.ts:55-58's removeMembers(id, userIds) discards userIds entirely and calls client.delete(`/api/v1/admin/groups/${id}/members`) with no body and no user_id in the path. No backend route matches that path -- the real backend route (routers/identity.ex:182, mounted at /identity per api_pipeline.ex:141) is /api/v1/identity/groups/:id/members/:user_id. The button as currently wired cannot remove a specific member's role at all. CODE-DESIGNER must either (a) design the web/ fix needed to make GroupsPage.tsx's removeMembers call actually reach the correct per-member DELETE route (this touches an owned_module, web/src/pages/admin/GroupsPage.tsx / web/src/api/identity.ts, already listed in this handoff's context.owned_modules, so it is in scope), or (b) identify a different already-working GUI path that performs single-role revocation and re-verify it against real source, or (c) explicitly scope AC2's role-revocation half to require a web/ fix as part of this requirement's implementation, not merely cite it as already-shipped. Re-submit with the corrected/verified GUI write path and updated §4 table.
